provenance: Root and delegated research checks in this conversation, including the continued agent check of the author-hosted October 6 entry-barriers paper. Reading depths vary and are recorded individually; sources were not all reread during publication.
billing_caveat: Extraction API zero does not include the current Codex conversation or research-tool billing; no all-in zero-cost claim is made.
core_candidate_question: How do employers change the content and substitutability of qualifying prior experience during AI diffusion, beyond required years, and do these changes correspond to changes in observed external entrants' backgrounds?
priority_claim: Not established. Broad first-ever claims on endogenous requirements, linked resume-posting data, and dynamic task measurement are contradicted by direct predecessors.

studies.authors: Alicia Sasser Modestino; Daniel Shoag; Joshua Ballance
studies.title: Downskilling: Changes in Employer Skill Requirements over the Business Cycle
studies.reading_scope: Author-provided published PDF: abstract/introduction, theory, experience definitions, results and conclusion; not claimed as a full close reading of all appendices.
studies.relevant_evidence: Labor-market tightness and employer education/experience requirements; within firm-job-title-county comparisons and a labor-supply-shock design.
studies.implication: Firms actively adjusting experience requirements to worker scarcity is not a new mechanism. Years-based requirements are not the same object as detailed substitutable experience pathways.

related_published_paper.title: Artificial Intelligence, Firm Growth, and Product Innovation

studies.reading_scope: Delegated checks of relevant data/method sections across the related papers; root checked the Berkeley research overview. No entire-paper or exact-ad-to-hire linkage claim.
studies.implication: Combining Cognism resumes and Burning Glass postings at firm level predates this project; dual-source data alone is not a first.

studies.title: Generative AI as Seniority-Biased Technological Change: Evidence from U.S. Resume and Job Posting Data
studies.reading_scope: Introduction and relevant data/method sections 4.2-4.3, including postings, employment flows and task mapping. Not a complete paper reading; no sample-size comparison across versions.
studies.relevant_evidence: Revelio resumes and postings; firm adoption signals, hires/separations/promotions, and junior task changes.
studies.implication: A very close predecessor. The project cannot claim to be first to combine resume and vacancy evidence of GenAI. Firm-level linkage is not an exact advertisement-person hiring link.

studies.title: Generative AI and Occupational Entry Barriers: The Labor-Supply Channel of Technological Change
studies.reading_scope: Author-hosted full text obtained after SSRN 403: abstract, introduction, section 4.1, section 6.2 and conclusion checked; not read page by page in full.
relevant_evidence: LLM-scored expertise requirements across 19,265 O*NET tasks, with and without GenAI assistance, produce potential supply shifts.
Observed occupational flows are used to calibrate transition costs; the paper is not devoid of real flow data.
Those flows are not a direct identification of changes in actual cross-industry entry following employer experience-clause changes.
The checked version fixes the task/occupation set and leaves actual entry changes as a future empirical question.
studies.implication: Potential labor-supply and entry-barrier mechanisms are not novel here. Direct employer-qualification and observed-entrant evidence remains a candidate distinct margin, not certified priority.
studies.metadata_caveat: Initial-version date differs between the PDF and indexed SSRN record; cite year and the checked October 6 revision rather than asserting one initial date.

studies.implication: Fine-grained dynamic vacancy task measurement is not a first. Working-paper estimates are not treated as settled causal results.

studies.title: The Skill Content of Recent Technological Change: An Empirical Exploration
studies.implication: Computerization affects routine cognitive as well as manual tasks and within-occupation content. The old-software-only-manual versus GenAI-only-cognitive dichotomy is not supported.

data_methodology.reading_scope: Relevant methodology on profile coverage, weighting, reporting lags and entity identifiers checked.
data_methodology.implication: Full vendor delivery is not a workforce census. Posting-derived expected hires can be predictions; they do not establish observed advertisement-to-person hiring links. Current project delivery and crosswalk readiness still require separate verification.

corrections: Recognized experience can be recombined rather than simply widened or narrowed.
Cross-industry and cross-occupation entry are important dimensions but not all experience transfer.
Common changes in tasks, qualifications and entrant composition do not establish a causal qualifications-to-hiring mechanism.
